newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
CONGRESS PARTY DECISION-MAKING AUTHORITY CHALLENGED

Loyalists of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao have challenged the authority of the Congress Working Committee (CWC), over the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP). They said that any decision taken by the CWC over the issue of a new CPP leader would not be binding on the CPP. The loyalists are pressing the party leadership to hold the election of a CPP leader by a secret ballot. The challenge has jolted the followers of Congress president Sitaram Kesri, who have been trying to effect a consensus in his favour.
The Economic Times
BANKS, FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS RAISE 60 BLN RUPEES

Banks, financial institutions and finance companies raised over 60 billion rupees in 1996 from the capital market, accounting for 55 percent of the total amount raised. Banks and institutions raised 45.8 billion rupees, while finance companies raised the rest. Sources said this trend would pick up further with more financial sector companies raising funds in the first half of 1997. There were 418 issues (35 percent) from the finance sector in 1996.
MATSUSHITA PUTS EXPANSION ON HOLD

Matsushita Electric Industrial Co, the world's largest consumer electronics company, has put its expansion plans in India on hold. Earlier, Matsushita had proposed investments of over $200 million in India. The bulk of this was to be in several manufacturing ventures, including those for white goods, compressors, auto insertion machinery, video cassette recorders and telecom equipment. It had also proposed increasing the paid-up capital of its flagship subsidiary, National Panasonic India, from 250 million to 400 million rupees. The plans were deferred because of the below-average response its products got in India and a slow-down in the consumer electronics market.
Financial Express
STRICTER MOTOR VEHICLES ACT ON ANVIL

The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, would be amended soon. The amended Act would incorporate wide ranging changes in the fee and penalty structure regulating the transport industry. Surface Transport Ministry sources said the changes in the Act were also expected to include specifications on safety parameters, fitness of vehicles, permit and licence conditions. The changes would either become applicable through a notification or with the consent of Parliament, sources added.
IOC IN MARKETING TIE-UP FOR RELIANCE PETRO PRODUCTS

The Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) has offered to market products from Reliance Petroleum Ltd's (RPL) Jamnagar refinery. The marketing tie-up will ensure that any market imbalances in distribution by public sector undertakings are controlled. The draft agreement signed by the two parties justifies the deal as the 15 million tonne refinery will have a market share equivalent to that of state-run Bharat Petroleum Corporation and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation.
CHAMBERS WANT TAX REDUCTION

Two industry chambers have asked the government to reduce the corporate tax rate from 40 percent to 30 percent in their pre-budget memoranda. The chambers also favoured the withdrawal or modification of Minimum Alternate Tax and scrapping double taxation on dividends. The chambers, Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and the Associated Chamber of Commerce (Assocham) also favoured reduction of the corporate tax rates to the international level of 25 percent over the next two to three years. They said dividends received in foreign exchange by Indian companies from abroad should be treated at par with export earnings.
JAPAN TO TAP INDIA'S SOFTWARE EXPERTISE

A consortium of five leading Japanese companies have floated an equity venture in collaboration with leading Indian hardware and software companies to outsource software from India. The project, promoted by Kenichi Ohmae, would be backed by the Japanese government, industry sources said. Initially, the project envisages outsourcing almost 17.5 billion rupees worth of software by the end of the current fiscal. The project does not involve any financial investment from Indian companies.
INFLATION RATE CROSSES SEVEN PERCENT

For the first time in the current 1996/97 (Aril-March) fiscal year, the year-on-year inflation rate based on the wholesale price index breached the seven percent mark to touch a year high of 7.08 percent for the week ended December 14. Annual inflation increased by 0.2 percentage points compared to 6.88 percent during the previous week. The wholesale price index went up by 0.1 percent to 319 points. The last time inflation rate had crossed the seven percent was in November 1995.
Business Standard
PROVISIONING NORMS FOR SMALL LOANS TIGHTENED

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has tightened the prudential norms on small loans. The central bank raised the ad-hoc provisioning requirement to 15 percent from 10 percent of the aggregate advances outstanding in this category on March 31, 1997. Advances under the small loans category are essentially exposures below 25,000 rupees and constitute about 15 percent of the total advances of the banking sector of roughly 450 billion rupees. The RBI has also granted a year's extension to all commercial banks for classifying the small loans and making provisions.
INDUSTRY WANTS CAP ON INSTITUTIONAL HOLDINGS

Industrialists have appealed to the finance ministry to cap financial institutions' (FI) holdings in companies at 20 percent. The proposal reflects their fear of FIs reversing their policy of supporting existing managements in disputes over control. A study conducted by an industry chamber shows leading financial institutions holdings to range between 35 and 65 percent of the total equity of many firms. With a liberalised takeover code in the offing, family-led groups are apprehensive of a sellout of FI holdings to raiding rivals.
VSNL DEMANDS ACTION AGAINST U.S. FIRMS

The feud between the U.S. telecommunication regulator, FCC, and the Indian monopoly service provider for international calls, VSNL, has escalated. VSNL has demanded action against U.S.-based carriers like Sprint, MCI and AT&T, for promoting call-back traffic from India. It asked the government to inform the U.S. regulator that call-back services, declared legal by the FCC, were illegal in India. The FCC had, earlier, refused to accept a letter from VSNL on this issue.
The Observer
CONTINUATION OF MINIMUM ALTERNATE TAX PROPOSED

The Ninth Five-Year Plan's (1997-2002) draft approach paper has called for making the minimum alternate tax more effective to yield additional revenue. It also suggested the introduction of an expenditure-based resumptive income tax. The draft, prepared by the Planning Commission, termed the non-payment of corporate tax by a number of companies as a serious issue and said the growing influx of unaccounted money was an impediment to growth of industry.
